episode.title: Keep cold session restoration inside the selected workspace's runtime storage context
episode.before: At parent 9b716cc0e61ffdd4967665d7c0e3c952cf06d7de, both the route-based and protocol-dispatched load/resume paths selected a workspace runtime and constructed a SessionService with that runtime's explicit base directory, but invoked the runtime bridge's loadSession or resumeSession outside a pinned ambient Storage context. Code reached through the bridge that called Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() could therefore observe the process/default runtime root instead of the selected workspace runtime root.
episode.after: At e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48, each complete load/resume critical section is executed through runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage using the selected runtime's sessionRuntimeBaseDir. The helper pins that root through Storage.runWithResolvedRuntimeBaseDir, so asynchronous restore work and bridge calls observe the selected workspace storage root. Tests cover load and resume through both route-based and protocol-dispatched entry points with distinct replacement or secondary runtime roots.
episode.diff: The route handler now wraps archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany and its full restore callback in runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(runtime, ...). The protocol dispatcher imports the same helper, extracts its coordinated restore callback as restoreInRuntime, and executes it through runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(sessionRuntime, restoreInRuntime). The helper's input type is narrowed to the sessionRuntimeBaseDir-bearing portion of a runtime. Two parameterized test groups create sessions under non-default runtime roots and assert that Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() equals the selected root while bridge loadSession or resumeSession executes.

evidence_units.claim: Commit e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48 has parent 9b716cc0e61ffdd4967665d7c0e3c952cf06d7de and is titled "fix(cli): restore sessions in selected workspace runtime (#9050)".
evidence_units.source: local git: git log -1 --format='%H%n%P%n%s%n%b' e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0]

evidence_units.claim: Storage.runWithResolvedRuntimeBaseDir installs an AsyncLocalStorage context containing the resolved directory with pinned=true; Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir gives this pinned context precedence over environment and process-level configuration.

In the parent route implementation, archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany directly enclosed the restore and bridge loadSession/resumeSession calls; the selected runtime was used for an explicitly configured SessionService, but no runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage context enclosed the operation.

The route-based restore path now calls runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(runtime, () => archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany(...)), placing session lookup, metadata recovery, bridge load/resume, relocation, and reconciliation within the selected runtime's pinned storage context.

In the parent protocol dispatcher, the coordinated restore callback invoked bridge loadSession/resumeSession without an enclosing runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage context, even though SessionService itself received sessionRuntime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir.

The protocol dispatcher now defines restoreInRuntime for the coordinated restore operation and invokes it with runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(sessionRuntime, restoreInRuntime), thereby enclosing bridge loadSession/resumeSession and related restore work in the selected runtime context.

runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage delegates to Storage.runWithResolvedRuntimeBaseDir using runtime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir; the change narrows its accepted runtime shape to Pick<WorkspaceRuntime, 'sessionRuntimeBaseDir'> without changing its runtime behavior.

The route-level parameterized test writes a session under a secondary runtime root, invokes both cold load and cold resume through the session route, spies on the selected bridge operation, and asserts that Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() observed during restoration equals secondaryRuntimeBaseDir and that the response succeeds.

The protocol-level parameterized test writes a session under a replacement runtime root, activates a replacement workspace runtime using that root, invokes session/load and session/resume, and asserts inside the bridge restore function that Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() equals replacementRuntimeBaseDir; it also checks a successful result and one restore invocation.
The commit modifies exactly the two restore call sites, the runtime-storage helper typing, and the two corresponding test files.

candidate_atomics.name: scope-route-restore-to-selected-runtime-storage
candidate_atomics.description: Execute the complete route-based cold load/resume operation inside the storage context owned by the selected workspace runtime.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent route-based session restoration from reading or creating runtime artifacts under a different workspace's or process-default storage root.
semantic_action.pre_state: A request has resolved a workspace runtime, but its coordinated restore callback and bridge load/resume execute without that runtime's pinned ambient storage context.
semantic_action.post_state: All storage resolution performed during the coordinated route restore, including asynchronous bridge work, observes the selected runtime's session storage root.
semantic_action.validation: For both cold load and cold resume, persist the target only under a distinct secondary runtime root, invoke the route, assert a successful response, and assert that the bridge observes that root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir().

candidate_atomics.name: scope-protocol-restore-to-selected-runtime-storage
candidate_atomics.description: Execute the complete protocol-dispatched cold load/resume operation inside the storage context owned by the selected workspace runtime generation.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent protocol-dispatched session restoration from falling back to the process/default storage root after selecting or replacing a workspace runtime.
semantic_action.pre_state: The dispatcher has selected a workspace runtime and explicitly configures one session service with its root, but bridge load/resume and other nested storage consumers run without a pinned ambient context.
semantic_action.post_state: The coordinated protocol restore and its bridge operations execute with the selected runtime root as the pinned ambient storage base directory.
semantic_action.validation: For both session/load and session/resume, activate a runtime replacement with a distinct root, store the target there, invoke the protocol request, and assert successful restoration plus the replacement root observed inside the bridge restore function.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-selected-runtime-context-across-session-restore
candidate_workflows.description: After routing a restore request to a workspace-specific runtime, propagate that runtime's storage root across the entire asynchronous restore boundary for every exposed restore entry point, then verify load and resume against deliberately distinct roots.

workflow_graph.goal: A cold session load or resume consistently reads and reconstructs state from the storage root owned by the runtime selected for the request.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Multiple workspace runtimes may use distinct storage roots; request routing selects the correct runtime, but one or more restore entry points do not preserve its ambient storage context through asynchronous bridge restoration.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every changed restore entry point encloses its full coordinated restore callback in the selected runtime's pinned storage context, and load/resume tests demonstrate that bridge code observes the selected non-default root.
